releases.body:
**OmO Native init-deep committed mode no longer dead-ends.** Committed mode now finishes through its own pull-request handoff instead of pointing at a skill that does not ship with OmO Native, and it reports how to finish by hand when no PR can be opened. Thanks to @HolisticDeveloper for the report and @surlymochan for the fix. ([#11228](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11228), fixes [#9686](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9686))

**The stale-reflection-lock test leaves no background writer behind when removing its temporary root.** Its teardown closes the memory wiring and awaits facts reconciliation and maintenance before removal, so a late lock publication cannot recreate the directory and make the temp-leak guard blame another test. ([#11225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11225))

**ulw-research ships a Markdown block model for checking Markdown and post deliverables.** It splits a Markdown report into headings, paragraphs, list items, table rows, code blocks and quotes with exact text offsets, and sorts sections with the same classifier as the HTML checks; an unclosed code fence is reported instead of passing silently, and no check uses it yet. The HTML checks now also treat a section headed exactly "Closing" as the closing section. ([#11153](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11153), part of [#11009](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11009))

**ulw-research ships checked polish edits and a polish diff for research reports.** Polish changes text nodes only: tags, every attribute, comments, and script/style/template content stay byte-identical, including attribute order and quoting. `polish-apply` rejects markup changes and edits that change a fact, number, unit, ticker, or required hedge, and checks cumulative edits against the original report; `polish-diff` applies the same rules to the whole report. An edit may not contain `<`, `>` or `&`, and may not touch a character reference even without them; both gates also compare the whole-document skeleton (every markup token and every character reference, byte for byte), so entities and markup are left untouched. Both gates refuse documents with markup the checker cannot model exactly. Markup changes require the full fidelity gates. Severities come from the defect registry. Nothing in the CLI calls them yet. ([#11152](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11152), part of [#11009](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11009))

**Re-extracting a conversation no longer counts the same agreement correction again.** Corrections are bound to validated user turns and recorded atomically with their replay receipts. Distinct turns on the same date still count separately; acknowledgement, drop and eviction retain replay history. Pending records from older versions use a documented agreement/date migration. ([#11214](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11214), fixes [#11191](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11191))

**The LSP MCP server negotiates supported protocol versions.** It preserves supported client versions and answers unsupported or missing versions with `2025-06-18`, rather than claiming an arbitrary protocol revision. ([#11208](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11208))

**Skill MCP tool errors are reported as errors.** Structured output and result metadata reach the caller, tool failures are not retried as connection failures, and plain content keeps its existing output format. ([#11207](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11207))

**The repository now has a security policy.** `SECURITY.md` explains how to report a vulnerability privately through GitHub's Security tab, what to include, and when to expect triage and an acknowledgement; `CONTRIBUTING.md` links to it. Adapted from the policy proposed by @marklapointe in [#10752](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-open

**Reading the end of a long session takes 42 ms and 68 MB instead of 40 s and 1.8 GB.** `session_read`, `session_search` and `session_info` page through OpenCode's message API instead of loading the whole session: on a 23,000-message session, `session_read` with `limit: 2, from_end: true` dropped from 39.6 s and 1,848 MB peak memory to 42 ms and 68 MB, and a search that runs out its 60-second timeout now stops reading when it returns, where it used to read another 228 MB in the background ([#10738](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10738), [#10741](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10741)).

**OmO's extension no longer carries an LSP engine it never runs.** The native LSP tools and post-edit diagnostics already go through the packaged LSP daemon, but the formatter's import pulled lsp-core's whole in-process engine into `omo.js`; importing only the helpers it uses shrinks the extension by about 82 KB, with no change in behavior. ([#10659](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10659))

**Every session start reads about 33 KB less of `omo.js`: eleven memory slash commands and memory sync's device account load on first use ([#10902](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10902), [#10860](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10860)).** The commands (`/memory`, `/remember`, `/init`, `/recompile`, `/memory-repository`, `/sleeptime`, `/reflect`, `/dream`, `/search`, `/facts`, `/agreements`) still appear at startup with the same names, descriptions and hints; their handlers load from `extensions/omo-memory-commands.js`. The signed-in device account loads from `extensions/omo-device-account.js` the first time a session resolves its sync, and if that file cannot load, memory sync reports `sync-unavailable` with the reason instead of looking signed out.

**ulw-research ships a fact ledger, a fidelity state file and a claim index for research reports.** They give each research run a machine-readable record of its facts and verified claims; nothing in the CLI uses them yet. ([#11046](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11046), part of [#11009](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/11009); batch [#11148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11148))

**Child-task, workflow and workpool wake sources report kind `children`.** ([#11114](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11114), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782))

**An unreadable workpool store no longer drops or falsely clears the children wake source.** ([#11118](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11118), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782))

**The children wake source reads the workpool store once per snapshot.** ([#11124](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11124), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782)) (batch [#11148](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11148))

**Child results waiting in the wake queue keep the parent from reading as done.** ([#11115](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11115), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782))

**The wake-queue count can no longer cost a delivery receipt and is re-published per session generation.** ([#11121](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11121), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782))

**A receipt that throws no longer leaves the wake-queue count up.** ([#11122](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11122), part of [#10782](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10782))

**Delivery receipts are isolated from each other, on retire too, and no receipt error is dropped.** ([#11123](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/11123), part of [#10782](https://github.

**The engine moves to senpi 2026.10.21-3: long 1M-context conversations stop re-writing their cached prefix, Anthropic subscription context is counted once, and "No credential slots available" no longer locks every account out ([#10965](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10965)).** When context reduction trims a long conversation on a 1M window, the reduced prefix now stays identical and keeps its cache checkpoint, so each step writes only what changed. Anthropic subscription turns with internal SDK re-requests no longer double the context percentage or start compaction early, and a configured compaction model now summarizes while your session provider is healthy, overflow recovery included. The subscription lane is the only layer that picks its accounts, so one revoked or briefly rate-limited account no longer blocks the rest until you log in again. Every turn end says what happens next, a turn-end report names the hold your queued message released, the trailing "Anything else? (optional)" card is gone from clients without native questions, and moving a session between machines runs through one implementation. Forced recovery after a context overflow no longer picks the same compaction cut again when an invisible entry leads the session; an overflow still never moves a task to its next fallback model.

```bash
bun add -g omo-ai
```

**A session's first prompt no longer freezes a shared host while it reads what changed in memory ([#10728](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10728)).** A session resumed a few hours after its last turn read the memory commits since then with one `git diff-tree` process per commit, all started at once. On a busy memory repository that was thousands of processes, and starting them blocked every session on the same host for 28 s with one session and 142 s with seven, while the finished ones piled up unreaped. The range is now read with one `git log`; the same notices come out, the longest block with seven sessions fell to 16 s, and the host's memory footprint during prompts fell from a median of 1,258 MB to 813 MB. ([#10726](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10726))

**Prompts stop freezing a shared host after every memory commit ([#10731](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10731)).** Recall skips memory notes the conversation already mentions, and it rechecked the last 200 messages against every note again after each memory commit, one note at a time. On a 7,500-note memory that took 1 to 1.7 s per session per prompt, with every session on the host waiting. Earlier answers now carry over and only notes the commit added are checked, so a recheck takes about 6 ms and the first check about 0.2 s; with seven sessions and a commit every 20 s, the host's blocked time fell from 185 s to 28 s over four and a half minutes. The notes skipped are unchanged. ([#10729](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10729))

**A relaunch's first prompt no longer recompiles your memory.** The compiled memory block and its size estimate are now saved by commit inside the memory repository's `.git` folder, never committed or synced, and read back on the next launch. On a 6,862-note memory this cut the memory step of a prompt from a median of about 178 ms to about 52 ms in the desktop app. A block built after a git read failed is used once and never saved. ([#10674](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10674))


**Anonymous usage stats now count how many accounts you have linked per provider.** `session_started` reports, per provider kind, how many accounts the engine lists for it (the same list the app's account list shows: signed-in accounts and environment-variable slots), used or not, as capped counts only, never an account name, email, token or value ([#10919](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10919)).

**The desktop app and `omo login` can share one device on a machine.** A new hidden `omo account` command (`show`, `adopt`, `token`, `export`, `forget`) lets the desktop use the same OS-keychain sign-in the CLI writes, so a machine counts as one device for memory sync and only one process ever refreshes its tokens. Secrets pass only on stdin and stdout, a refused renewal (exit 5) names the service's refusal code so the desktop can say why the sign-in ended, and a locked OS keychain is reported as its own outcome (exit 7) instead of a generic failure. On Linux, where a locked Secret Service collection reads as empty, the default collection's lock state is read over D-Bus before any secret call (libsecret would otherwise ask the keyring to show an unlock prompt), a locked collection is reported (exit 7) instead of read, and when that check cannot answer (no `gdbus` on a minimal install, no Secret Service on the bus, a slow bus) the CLI prints one notice and uses libsecret directly as before, so login never depends on `gdbus` ([#10658](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10658)).

**Memory sync can join a new device.** `omo sync enable` turns memory sync on for the device and, if the account already syncs, asks a device that already syncs to approve it. `omo sync approve` on that device answers the request. Both screens show the same 6-digit code, and the new device is admitted only after the person confirms the codes match. A

**Memory sync checks each new keyring entry without re-reading the chain before it.** The client now uses the shared receiver's incremental entry point (omo-service #600, re-vendored), and the receiver moves along with the verified chain state. Appending one entry to a 1,000-entry chain used to hand the receiver all 1,006 entries again; it now hands it one, at any chain length. What the receiver refuses is unchanged, including a replayed or lower-seq entry. ([#10694](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10694), fixes [#10655](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10655))

**The engine moves to senpi 2026.10.21-2: idle task hosts exit again, reopened sessions stop spending quota, and sessions share their prompt cache ([#10893](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10893)).** A monitor watch no longer keeps every task shard host on the machine running, so idle hosts exit as designed. Reopening an unattended session no longer spends quota on goals or background events until you send input or choose Resume. Responses prompt-cache keys follow the model, instructions and tool schemas instead of the session, so new sessions and task children with the same prefix reuse one cache. A goal waiting on a subscription limit retries at the provider's reset time instead of hammering the spent account. On Windows, input sent while a turn is running no longer gets stuck or races through the whole fallback chain. Switching a long conversation to a smaller-context model while the current one is at its limit now applies at the next message, saving an API key over an OAuth login (or the reverse) replaces the credential instead of storing one that is never used, a busy command monitor is no longer muted after 200 lines a day, and every assistant reply records its timing (time to first token and generation rate).

**OmO records when an answer says "tests pass" or "done" with nothing in the session behind it.** When a turn's final answer says tests pass, a build or typecheck is clean, a feature already exists, or the work is done, OmO checks the session for a check that passed after the last code edit, and records in the session whether the claim is backed. It starts in shadow mode: nothing is shown to you or the agent and no turn is blocked or continued, because on a week of our own sessions most flags were still false positives. Setting the `omo-senpi-claim-receipt-nudge` flag turns on a short note under a flagged answer (once per message you send) and passes the flagged claims to a gate reviewer spawned afterwards. ([#10785](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10785))

**`omo doctor --models` shows which model every task category and agent runs, and `exclude_models` keeps a model out of all of them ([#10763](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10763)).** The new doctor view prints, per category and agent, the model a spawn runs first, the retry chain in order, and each rung's source (built-in, omo.json, or the category an agent borrows) with why it does or does not run: excluded, no login, or not reached. It reads the same resolvers spawns use, and `--json` gives the same view to scripts. The new top-level `exclude_models` list (`provider/model`, a bare model id, or a `*` pattern such as `"claude-fable-*"`) is honored by category and agent chains, memory children (the session model they would inherit included), the main session's model profile, explicit task pins, and task children respawned or resumed on a recorded model, including their recorded fallback chains. Before, no setting could stop a builtin rung from running; only logging out of its provider did (#10759).

**Geeky becomes Obsessive.** The two GPT lanes' display names are now Obsessive · Normal and Obsessive · Heavy, with one-line descriptions to match and a shared caution, NOT RECOMMENDED FOR WRITING OR EVERYDAY WORK., that the session-start notice renders in bold; the `geeky-normal` and `geeky-heavy` ids
